name: Dimension-Four Antipodal Trichotomy
statement: Let $G$ be a finite partial cube of isometric dimension four whose medium admits a closed orientation. If $G$ has an antipodal pair but is not a learning-space graph, then $G$ is isomorphic to exactly one of $\mathcal V_4$, $\mathcal Z_4$, and $\mathcal T_4$. Equivalently, a convex subgraph $C$ of a learning-space graph with $\operatorname{idim}(C)\le4$ is learning exactly when it has a $C$-antipodal pair and is not one of these three exceptions. The six possible closed oriented normal forms collapse to those three underlying graphs.
proof: A closed orientation gives a well-graded union-closed positive-content family without the empty state. Classifying it by the number of present singletons leaves six rootless oriented normal forms. Coordinate translations and permutations identify three with $\mathcal V_4$, two with $\mathcal T_4$, and one with $\mathcal Z_4$; all other cases admit an explicit translated root. Convex restrictions inherit the closed orientation.
